Store $FF in $EA50 for the actor in slot X.
Initialize LEVELG actor type $29 in slot X. Store $02 in horizontal extent, vertical extent. Store $FF in $EA50.

Initialize LEVELG actor type $32 in slot X. Store $09 in horizontal extent. Store $10 in vertical extent, horizontal movement. Store $03 in $E9F0. Set the vertical overlap extent at $EA80 and the separate sprite colour at $E930 to five. Store $0F in $E870.
Clear visibility bit $40 in the actor's flags.
Set extents ten and nineteen and $E9F0 and $EA80 to two. Set movement to eight, enable direct shape selection and set colour twelve.
Set extents to eleven and nineteen and $E9F0 and $EA80 to two. Set colour fourteen.
Set extents two and three and $EA50 to $FF. Copy nonzero low flag bits to $E840 and clear them in the flags.
Add bit $20 to the actor flags and jump to the initializer store at $C453.
Initialize LEVELG actor type $25 in slot X. Apply $20 with OR to actor flags.
Set $EA50 to $FF and both extents to three. If any of the low three flag bits are set, save them in $E840 and clear them.
Write extents three and two, then run $C3E5, which overwrites both extents with three.
Write extents two and ten, then run $C3E5, which makes both extents three.
Set colour fourteen, $E9C0 to $14, bit $10 at $EB10 and extents to sixteen and twenty-one. Clear $EA80 for the slot and store four at the fixed $E9F0 address.

Initialize LEVELG actor types $27, $28 in slot X. Store $01 in horizontal extent, vertical extent. Apply $34 with OR to actor flags. Apply $01 with OR to shape and actor flags at $EB10. Store $FF in $EA50. Store $0A in $E870.
Set movement five and extents $24 and $3F. Clear $E9F0, $EA80, $1D, $1F and $E9C0. Apply $C4E6 and allocate types $2B through $30, copying the parent's coordinates and saving its slot in each child.
Clear $E840 and set $E870 to $40 before the common linked-actor initializer at $C4E6.
Initialize LEVELG actor types $2B, $2C, $2D, $2E, $2F in slot X. Store $0E in sprite colour. Store $FF in $EA50. Apply $10 with OR to actor flags.
Set flag $10 and coarse Y three, then clear visibility bit $40.
Set $E9F0 and $EA80 to two and extents ten and fifteen. Set $EA50 to $FF and hide the actor at $C36F.
Write extent two then three, and jump to $C3E5 for the common setup that overwrites both with three.
Enter at the horizontal-extent store with A equal to three, then continue through the common extent and flag initialization.

Initialize LEVELG actor type $31 in slot X. Store $0A in horizontal extent. Store $12 in vertical extent. Store $03 in $E9F0, $EA80. Enable direct sprite shape selection by setting bit $80 at $EB10. Store $05 in sprite colour. Apply $04 with OR to actor flags. Store $0F in $E870.
Initialize LEVELG actor type $34 in slot X. Store $04 in sprite colour. Store $00 in $E870.

Set horizontal movement to $10. Require carry clear from $275A, $E840 zero and a successful $2760 check with ten. When the random byte is also zero, request type $27 through $28AF. Then enter the turn logic with four in $08.
Call $287A only when the glyph animation phase is zero.
If flag $04 is clear, toggle direction bit $08 and set $04. Then call $2757 with four.
Return immediately from the actor callback. The corresponding descriptor slot passes control through $15EB and this RTS returns to the engine.

Decrement the timer at $C64C. When it underflows, reload $0A and advance the phase at $C64D modulo four. Copy 32 bytes backwards into $7960–$797F, replacing glyphs $2C–$2F in the playfield character set.
The four phase offsets $1F, $3F, $5F and $3F point to the last byte of each 32-byte animation frame relative to $C5EC. The copying loop counts down from the selected end.
Four consecutive eight-byte glyph bitmaps for animation phase 0. This frame replaces playfield glyphs $2C–$2F.
Four consecutive eight-byte glyph bitmaps for animation phase 1 and 3. This frame replaces playfield glyphs $2C–$2F.
Four consecutive eight-byte glyph bitmaps for animation phase 2. This frame replaces playfield glyphs $2C–$2F.
Countdown in calls to the stage update. Underflow reloads it with $0A and advances the animation phase.
The update increments this value modulo four and uses it to index the backwards-copy offsets at $C5E8.

On carry from $22E5 advance a coarse row and call $381A. When $E840 is zero, remove the actor. Otherwise use $E840 plus $1A as the replacement type, remapping $20 to zero and subtracting nine coarse rows. Call $3854 and clear removal before checking player proximity. A success chooses the $27DA argument by relative coarse X.
Call $287A and $2757 with six, then count $E9C0 down. On underflow reload it to $50 and attempt to spawn four shots when $2760 succeeds.
Mirror its flags and horizontal extent to $7D and $7E. Count $E870 down, removing the actor when negative and running $287A otherwise.
Allocate four actors using $C706. Give the first two opposing vertical movements and the latter two horizontal magnitude $40, toggling direction for the fourth.
Allocate type $28, set its $E870 timer to ten and copy its parent's coordinates.

Put the current slot into the child at $C97C as its $E8A0 reference. Call $38BD. While $390C is clear use $23B7 to select colour fourteen or one and check $275A. On carry set $390C to $14, restore type $2A and clear visibility. Other paths call $2742 with six and toggle direction on $E9C0 underflow.
Copy the parent's position and add three to coarse X. Then run the shared shape and parent checks.
Copy the parent's coordinates with $0280 added to the two-byte Y coordinate.
Copy the parent coordinates with coarse X plus three and two-byte Y plus $0280.
Copy the parent's coordinates, using ADC with five on coarse Y and preserving incoming carry in the addition.
Copy the parent's coordinates with three added to coarse X, then apply ADC with five to coarse Y using the carry from X. Fall through to the shared animation and checks.
Update the shape with $2742 and run $287A. Copy the parent colour and remove the child if $390C is set, the parent has changed type from $2A, or its flags show removal.
Jump around the final parent check to the return at $C844.
Remove the child when the parent flags are zero or bit zero is set. Otherwise return.
If $1F is set increment sprite colour and set visibility. Test each active player unless $1D is negative. Carry from $23D6 calls $216F and flags the actor for removal.

When $1D is nonzero copy its low seven bits to $70 and set $1E to three. Allocate type $25, set the original actor's coarse Y to four and transfer its position to the new slot. Flag the original for removal, call $3854 on the new actor and set $4F to $FF.
Run $2757 with six and count $E870 down. A negative result reloads it to $28 and requests a type $27 actor through $28AF, which can mark the new slot for removal after its distance checks.

When $E750 reaches zero reload it to two and advance the phase modulo four. Choose a group offset from signed vertical or nonzero horizontal movement and direction, combine it with the phase and read $C8FE before continuing to $C575.
Four groups of four sprite pointers for negative vertical, positive vertical and the two horizontal directions in the actor shape cycle.

Call the resident contact and shape checks and save this slot at $C97C. Use $E840 and $E870 as indices into $5300. Scale each sample by eight, add it to the corresponding coordinate of the actor indexed by $E8A0 and subtract four from the coarse X result. Advance both indices by four and run the shared link check.
The orbiting actor saves its own slot here. The parent update uses that slot to write its own index to the child's $E8A0 field.
